newsitem.title: UK: Channel Tunnel rail link operator invites bids.
newsitem.headline: Channel Tunnel rail link operator invites bids.

text.p: London & Continental Railways (LCR), the developer of the Channel Tunnel rail link between London and the coast, said on Sunday it was inviting tenders for five tunnelling contracts worth 800 million pounds.

The 68-mile (108 km) high-speed rail link between London and the Channel Tunnel has been beset by long delays because of arguments over its route, but LCR said it was delighted to report that preparatory engineering work had begun.

LCR said it had already received the first bid for the single largest tunnelling contract, worth 300 million pounds, which involves building the Stratford station box in east London and twin tunnels from north London's Islington to Barking.

The company said it expected to announce the first contractor for the main tunnelling work by late summer. The remaining 500 million pounds of contracts are scheduled to be tendered over the next three months.

With construction expected to begin in 1998, LCR hopes the new tunnels will reduce passenger journey times to Paris and Brussels by 35 minutes as well as substantially cutting the times for domestic journeys from the south eastern English county of Kent.
LCR is owned by a consortium including Bechtel, SBC Warburg, Virgin Group, National Express Group Plc and London Electricity Plc.
